svg.text: A chain running straight down the page: each part demonstrates, with a different kind of system, that the previous
part's exact failure also shows up here — culminating in computational irreducibility as the one explanation for
all of it, before the final part asks what can still be done in practice.

g.text: A chain of mounting evidence (Turing machines, cellular automata, proofs, mathematics) converges on computational
irreducibility as the root cause of bugs, then diverges into practical responses.

g.title: Why do simple programs misbehave? — → spya-d46wsq
n+1 machine fails at n=7 — extra scribbling on 111-endings — → spya-h3jx6h
Bugs can hide for arbitrarily many steps — first bug at n=15, n=63... — → spya-pt0hmz
g.text: Bugs can hide for arbitrarily many steps

g.title: Whatever you specify, some machine insidiously violates it — → spya-jdmx0m
A doubling rule fails suddenly at n=14 — → spya-htqcgc
g.text: A doubling rule fails suddenly at n=14

g.title: Can we tell in advance? — → spya-gt6430
Sometimes yes: rule 122 analysis proves no bug possible — → spya-gagsuk
Symbolic axioms + induction formally prove a machine bug-free — → spya-q8fg9q
A buggy machine yields no proof, however long you search — → spya-ypka68
g.text: A buggy machine yields no proof, however long

g.title: Computational irreducibility: behavior can only be known by running it — → spya-wcnws7
g.text: behavior can only be known by

g.title: So testing can't guarantee a bug won't surface later — → spya-yc9e2z
g.text: So testing can't guarantee a bug won't surface

g.title: Rule 30, long halts, broken symmetry — → spya-kjsjh5
Even mathematics finds late counterexamples — → spya-cc855a
Good language design & visualization push the frontier back, but never erase it — → spya-kdks69
g.text: Good language design & visualization push the
frontier back, but never erase it
A chain: a minimal failure, a census of when such failures first appear, an especially hidden case, and the same

g.title: 3-state machine seems to compute n+1 — → spya-scjxv8
Fails at n=7: outputs 9 instead of 8 — head 'scribbles' on 111-endings — → spya-h3jx6h
g.text: Fails at n=7: outputs 9 instead of 8

g.title: 8934 machines correctly compute n+1 — some simple, some wildly nested — → spya-rhc6t0
Census of where first bugs appear — → spya-y7nwnj
g.text: Census of where first bugs appear

g.title: One machine works flawlessly for n=0..14, then fails at n=15 — → spya-pt0hmz
4-state machine: correct for all n up to 62, fails at 63 — → spya-hqukdz
g.text: 4-state machine: correct for all n up

g.title: Highest-risk inputs: binary numbers of all 1s (2^i - 1) — → spya-u3d2ws

g.text: A fork, not a settled question: one path of careful structural reasoning proves a system bug-free, while the
formal-proof path for Turing machines only succeeds exactly when there is in fact no bug to find.

g.title: Some patterns are visibly bug-free — → spya-rhda0x
A complex-looking rule survives 100,000 tests — but fluctuations leave doubt — → spya-asw9eq
Studying the whole computation, not just outputs — rind always moves left or stays — → spya-r7ty6m
g.text: rind always moves left or stays

g.title: Interior dynamics = known rule 122 — → spya-gagsuk
Rule 122 can never die out → pattern must stabilize, no bug — → spya-n5acnw
g.text: Rule 122 can never die out → pattern

g.title: Separately: symbolic axioms + induction prove a Turing machine correct — → spya-q8fg9q
Proof search = path through a multiway graph of theorems — → spya-bn24t3
g.text: Proof search = path through a multiway

g.title: For a buggy machine, no path exists — the claim is false — → spya-ypka68
g.text: For a buggy machine, no path exists —
